Overstock — real days-of-cover

On-hand ÷ (6-month trailing outbound qty ÷ 180). Outbound = dispensed (DS) + sent on transfer (TS) — Riyadh Main Store is the central purchasing/storage hub for all 4 branches, so stock leaving there via transfer is real movement too, not just what it dispenses locally. Flagged when >365 days of cover, or zero outbound movement in 6 months and not received within that same window (a fresh delivery isn't "dead stock" yet). The ERP's own MIN/MAX default is shown for comparison only — see finding below.

Slow-moving & dead stock

No outbound movement (dispense or transfer-out) in 90+ days as of the data snapshot, and not received (purchased or transferred in) within that same 90 days — a recent delivery hasn't had time to prove it's slow. Overlaps the overstock list but is tracked separately.

Expiry risk

Real batch-level balances (batch tracking is populated for this tenant) — not a receipt-date proxy. Each batch is valued at the same moving-average unit cost used for on-hand valuation, so you can see both the location and the SAR size of expiry risk.

Value at risk by branch

Receiving / data-quality flags

Single receipt lines >20× (or <1/20×) that product's own trailing median receipt quantity — a signature of a mis-keyed unit or quantity at receiving, not necessarily a real event.

Aging bucket — never dispensed

On-hand stock that has never once been dispensed (DS) from its current store, aged from its last purchase or transfer-in receipt to the data snapshot date. Some items only ever move between warehouses on a transfer without ever reaching a clinic — toggle to the "all branches" scope below to isolate those: zero dispense activity anywhere in the company for that SKU.

Price & Vendor Watch-list

The one-off price-gap and single-source findings, turned into a list to work down. Every alert is a real purchase-invoice pattern ranked by how many riyals it cost over the last 90 days. Set a status on each one (saved for everyone who opens this dashboard); the next refresh then shows what is new, what got worse, what cleared, and flags anything marked resolved that is still happening.

Open SAR impact, re-computed at each weekly cut

Each point re-runs the same rules on the purchases known at that date, so the line shows whether the problem is growing. The earliest points have less history behind them and read lower for that reason.

Alerts, largest first

Price changes between invoices — same product, same supplier

Every time a supplier invoices the same product at a different net price from its previous invoice — any size of change, up or down. Each row opens both invoices side by side: the purchase-invoice number, the supplier's own invoice number, and the scanned copy attached to it in the ERP. Use it to confirm a rise was agreed, or that a drop is not a unit-of-measure slip.

Prices are net per primary unit (unit-of-measure differences between invoices are already normalised) and volume-weighted when one invoice carries the product on several lines. SAR effect = (newer price − earlier price) × units on the newer invoice. “Check entry” marks moves of 3× or more, which are usually a keying or unit slip rather than a real price change. “Superseded” means a later invoice exists for the same product and supplier. Scan links open the PDF on the share (X:\VOUCHERS_DOCUMENTS — the January–May scans sit in its PI sub-folder). “Not linked in ERP” marks an invoice whose scan is on the share but has no attachment record in the ERP, which is every invoice before 31 March 2026; see the attachment alert further down.

Purchase returns and item-identity review

Returns. When a supplier invoices the wrong item or price and the purchase is sent back, the returned quantity is taken out of every price test above — it is not a price rise, a price drop or a cheaper-supplier gap. The changes this removes are listed at the bottom so nothing disappears silently.
Item identity. A line can also be received into the ERP under another item's code because the right item was not set up yet, then returned and re-bought. The ERP keeps no supplier item description, so the name on the supplier's invoice can only be compared on the scan; the list below ranks every returned line by how much it looks like that case (price far from the product's usual, returned in full, stock already moved before the return) so the scans worth opening first are at the top.

A return is matched to its purchase invoice through the invoice number on the return document (all 22 returns of 2026 are linked). Each flag scores a point (price far from the usual scores two, and a line of SAR 0 or more scores one more); High = four points or more, Medium = two or three. “Price vs usual” compares the price paid with the median of the product's other 2026 invoices, or with the cost the ERP used on later stock movements when there are fewer than two. “Moved before return” counts dispense and transfer-out quantity between the receipt and the return, product-wide, so it can include other stores. None of the 34 returned lines carries a reason on the return document — making the reason a required field would let this list separate supplier errors from item-code mix-ups without opening a scan.

Price changes left out because the quantity was returned

Not counted in any figure above

Purchase invoices vs attached scans

Each 2026 purchase invoice is set against the scan file attached to it. The scan normally holds the ERP receiving-voucher print and the supplier's own invoice. Where the text could be read, the scan was screened automatically for the supplier invoice number, the invoice total and the voucher number printed on it (the card below says on how many); the invoices most at risk (returned lines, price outliers, the largest values, suppliers with earlier findings) and two random samples were also read line by line by AI, comparing the supplier's item description, quantity and price with what was entered. The ERP stores no supplier item description, so this is the only way to see an item entered under another item's name — the cost then follows the wrong item.

Priority adds points for what the checks found: an AI-read difference of item, quantity or price (3–4), a printed voucher number that is not this invoice (3), supplier invoice number not found on the scan (2), total not found (1), scan unreadable (1), none of the ERP item names found (1), returned lines (1); High = 4 or more, Medium = 2–3. A read by AI that matches clears the automatic doubts. “Not found on the scan” often means a photographed or Arabic page that the automatic read could not decode, so open the scan before concluding. The supplier's invoice can show a discount that the ERP total does not (the total is gross); such gaps are noted but not treated as errors on their own. The AI read covers the priority invoices only, not every invoice.

Suppliers — where spend is moving

Last 90 days against the 90 days before. A supplier whose share jumps, or that appears for the first time, is worth a look even when none of its prices has tripped an alert.

Sole-source items bought in the last 90 days

Products with a single supplier on record for 2026, ranked by recent spend, with the price trend. With no second supplier there is no price to compare against, so a rise here is the one you cannot spot from the cheaper-supplier alerts.
How the numbers are built, and what they cannot tell you. Source: posted purchase-invoice lines from the ERP (all booked at Riyadh, the only branch that buys). Unit costs are net of line discounts — checked against VAT on 200 discounted lines. Price increase: same product and supplier, volume-weighted price in the last 90 days at least 10% above its average earlier in 2026; SAR = price rise × units bought in the last 90 days. Cheaper supplier: price paid at one supplier at least 10% above the lowest volume-weighted price among suppliers used in the last 180 days; SAR = the difference × units; it assumes the cheaper supplier has the same item and can supply the volume, and the row says when it was last used. Price entry check: a line priced above 3× or below ⅓ of the product's median — above, the figure is the amount paid over the median; below, it is the recorded line value (usually a unit-of-measure slip). Alerts under SAR 300 are not shown, and lines with zero cost or quantity are left out. SAR is not additive across types (a rise and a cheaper-supplier gap can describe the same purchases), so the headline counts each product-supplier pair once at its larger figure. There is no contract or tender price list in the data, so a rise that was agreed shows up as an alert — mark it Accepted. Freight, payment terms, rebates and invoice-level discounts are not modelled.

    Fraud & Control Detection

    Exception-based review across 4 categories, each grounded in fields actually present in the raw extract (created_by / posted_by / post_date vs. transaction_date / status / supplier). A flag marks a pattern worth a second look — it is not on its own a finding of wrongdoing.

    How a transfer is posted — and what that means for these flags

    Verified against the ERP's send / receive transfer documents (2026 to date). Transfers are the largest source of false signals in the checks below, so they are read through this workflow first.
